mainTopic: Whether רבי שמעון can follow רבי עקיבא's view that a seller sells generously (עין יפה), tested through a ברייתא about consecrating trees together with the land around them.
overview: The גמרא challenges the suggestion that רבי שמעון follows רבי עקיבא, who says a seller sells generously (עין יפה). It brings a ברייתא about consecrating trees. If a person consecrates three trees planted in orchard spacing (ten per בית סאה), the land and the young trees between them are consecrated too. He redeems the land at the Torah's fixed rate. If the spacing is different, the land is not included. The same is true if he consecrates the trees one after the other: he redeems only the trees, at their value. The גמרא shows this ברייתא cannot follow רבי עקיבא or the רבנן, since both say a consecrator gives generously. So it must be רבי שמעון. It then proves that רבי שמעון agrees with the רבנן that a seller is sparing (עין רעה), and he holds that a consecrator is sparing too and keeps the land. So רבי שמעון cannot be explained as following רבי עקיבא.

steps.title: Can רבי שמעון really follow רבי עקיבא? A ברייתא about three trees
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא questions whether רבי שמעון can follow רבי עקיבא. It brings a ברייתא: consecrating three trees planted ten to a בית סאה also consecrates the land and the trees between them.
steps.simpleTranslation: Can you really explain רבי שמעון as following רבי עקיבא? But a ברייתא teaches: if someone consecrates three trees planted at a rate of ten per בית סאה, he has also consecrated the land and the trees between them. So when he redeems them, he pays the Torah's fixed rate of fifty silver shekels for every area that takes a חומר of barley seed.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא opens a challenge against the idea that רבי שמעון agrees with רבי עקיבא. It starts quoting a ברייתא that it will use as ammunition.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Three trees in normal orchard spacing count as an orchard, so the land comes along with them. Because the land is included, he redeems it at the Torah's fixed rate for land, not by the value of the trees. This first clause is only background; the challenge comes from the cases in the next steps.

keyTerms.meaning: Can you really set up (explain) it as…?
He consecrated (gave to the Temple treasury)
An area of land that takes one סאה of seed
An area that takes a חומר of barley seed, redeemed at the Torah's fixed price

phrases.english: But can you really establish it
that Rabbi Shimon follows Rabbi Akiva?
phrases.notes: This goes back to the earlier suggestion that רבי שמעון holds like רבי עקיבא, who says a seller sells generously.

phrases.english: But isn't it taught in a baraita:
If one consecrated three trees
from a planting of ten per beit se'a,
phrases.notes: That is normal orchard spacing, so the three trees count as part of an orchard.

phrases.english: he has consecrated the land
and the trees between them;
therefore, when he redeems,
he redeems each area for sowing a chomer of barley
for fifty silver shekels.

steps.triggerLanguage: וּמִי מָצֵית מוֹקְמַתְּ לַהּ לְרַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן כְּרַבִּי עֲקִיבָא? וְהָא תַּנְיָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the earlier suggestion (before this section) that רבי שמעון follows רבי עקיבא.
steps.kashyaTarget: The claim that רבי שמעון holds like רבי עקיבא.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A ברייתא that, as the next steps show, can only be רבי שמעון rules that a consecrator does not include the land. That only makes sense if he does not hold like רבי עקיבא.

steps.title: Different spacing or one tree at a time: the land is not included
steps.stepSummary: If the trees are planted more densely or more sparsely, or are consecrated one after another, neither the land nor the young trees are consecrated. He redeems only the trees, at their value.
steps.simpleTranslation: If the trees were planted more densely or more sparsely than that, or he consecrated them one after the other, he has not consecrated the land or the trees between them. So when he redeems, he redeems the trees at their actual value.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא continues with the key cases: when the land does not come along with the trees.
steps.deeperAnalysis: With different spacing the trees are not a real orchard, so no orchard land comes along with them. The key case is consecrating them one after the other: even in orchard spacing, he holds back the land and gives only what he named, a sparing reading (עין רעה). The גמרא uses that case to identify whose opinion the ברייתא follows.

keyTerms.term: פָּחוֹת מִכָּאן אוֹ יוֹתֵר עַל כֵּן
keyTerms.meaning: Less than this or more than this (here: denser or sparser planting)

phrases.aramaic: פָּחוֹת מִכָּאן אוֹ יוֹתֵר עַל כֵּן,
phrases.english: If less than this or more than this,
or he consecrated them one after the other,

phrases.aramaic: הֲרֵי זֶה לֹא הִקְדִּישׁ לֹא הַקַּרְקַע,
phrases.english: then he has not consecrated the land
nor the trees between them.
Therefore, when he redeems,
he redeems the trees at their value.

steps.triggerLanguage: פָּחוֹת מִכָּאן אוֹ יוֹתֵר עַל כֵּן, אוֹ שֶׁהִקְדִּישָׁן בָּזֶה אַחַר זֶה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the ברייתא with the contrasting cases where the land is not included.
steps.raayaObject: Shows that this ברייתא reads consecration sparingly: the consecrator holds back the land.

steps.title: Even if he later consecrates the land, the trees are redeemed separately
steps.stepSummary: Even if he consecrated the trees and afterwards the land, he redeems the trees at their value and then the land at the fixed Torah rate.
steps.simpleTranslation: Moreover, even if he consecrated the trees and then went back and consecrated the land, when he redeems he pays for the trees at their value. Then he redeems the land at fifty silver shekels for every area that takes a חומר of barley seed.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא adds a stronger case. Even when everything ends up consecrated, the trees and the land are still treated as two separate gifts.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Since the earlier consecration of the trees did not include the land, the trees stand on their own. When the land is consecrated later, it is a separate act with its own price. This confirms that the land was never pulled in with the trees.

keyTerms.meaning: And not only that, but even more
And then went back and consecrated (a second act)

phrases.english: And not only that, but
even if he consecrated the trees,
phrases.notes: He means the trees in the cases just mentioned: different spacing, or one tree at a time.

phrases.english: and then went back and consecrated the land;
when he redeems,
he redeems the trees at their value,
and then redeems each area for sowing
a chomer of barley for fifty silver shekels.

steps.whatToRemember: In the ברייתא, consecrating trees one at a time (or not in orchard spacing) does NOT include the land. The consecrator holds the land back.
steps.triggerLanguage: וְלֹא עוֹד, אֶלָּא אֲפִילּוּ הִקְדִּישׁ אֶת הָאִילָנוֹת, וְחָזַר וְהִקְדִּישׁ אֶת הַקַּרְקַע
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds a stronger case to the ברייתא's rule from step 2.
steps.raayaObject: Strengthens the point that the land is not included with the trees.

steps.title: Whose opinion is the ברייתא? Not רבי עקיבא and not the רבנן
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks who wrote the ברייתא. It rules out רבי עקיבא, who says even a seller is generous, and the רבנן, who say a consecrator is generous.
steps.simpleTranslation: Whose view is this? If it is רבי עקיבא, he says a seller sells generously, and all the more so one who consecrates! If it is the רבנן, they say only a seller sells sparingly, but one who consecrates does so generously!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא tries to identify the author of the ברייתא by ruling out the opinions in the משנה one by one.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא has the consecrator holding back the land. רבי עקיבא would include the land, since for him even a seller gives generously. The רבנן would also include it, since they agree that a consecrator gives generously.

keyTerms.meaning: With a generous eye: the transfer includes more
With a sparing eye: the transfer includes only what was clearly stated

phrases.english: Whose view is this?
If it is Rabbi Akiva, doesn't he say:
a seller sells generously;
and all the more so one who consecrates!
If it is the Rabbis, don't they say:
it is a seller who sells sparingly,
but one who consecrates consecrates generously!

steps.confusionAlert: Don't mix up the two sides. רבי עקיבא is generous for BOTH a seller and a consecrator. The רבנן are sparing for a seller but generous for a consecrator. Neither fits a consecrator who holds back the land.
steps.triggerLanguage: מַנִּי? אִי רַבִּי עֲקִיבָא, הָא אָמַר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Analyzes the ברייתא quoted in steps 1-3 to find its author.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Which תנא's view matches the ברייתא's sparing reading of consecration?

steps.title: So the ברייתא must be רבי שמעון
steps.stepSummary: Since neither רבי עקיבא nor the רבנן fit, the ברייתא must follow רבי שמעון.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, it is obvious that this is רבי שמעון.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא concludes that the ברייתא follows רבי שמעון, the only remaining opinion.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In the משנה, רבי שמעון holds that one who consecrates a field does not include extras like the cistern and winepress. That matches the ברייתא's sparing reading of consecration.

phrases.english: Rather, it is obvious that it is Rabbi Shimon.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 4 by elimination.

steps.title: Which view about selling does רבי שמעון follow?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks whether רבי שמעון follows רבי עקיבא or the רבנן about a seller. It rules out רבי עקיבא, because then a consecrator would surely be generous.
steps.simpleTranslation: And which view does רבי שמעון follow? If he follows רבי עקיבא, רבי עקיבא says a seller sells generously, and all the more so one who consecrates!
steps.whatsHappening: Now that the ברייתא is רבי שמעון, the גמרא checks his view about a seller. This is the step that brings the original challenge home.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If רבי שמעון agreed with רבי עקיבא that a seller is generous, he would surely say a consecrator is generous too. But in the ברייתא, רבי שמעון's consecrator holds back the land. So he cannot follow רבי עקיבא.

phrases.english: And Rabbi Shimon, according to whose view?

phrases.aramaic: אִי אַלִּיבָּא דְרַבִּי עֲקִיבָא, הָא אָמַר:
phrases.english: If according to Rabbi Akiva, doesn't he say:
a seller sells generously;
and all the more so one who consecrates!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Builds on step 5's identification of רבי שמעון to test the original claim from step 1.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Does רבי שמעון agree with רבי עקיבא or with the רבנן about a seller?

steps.title: רבי שמעון follows the רבנן and holds that a consecrator also gives sparingly
steps.stepSummary: רבי שמעון must follow the רבנן that a seller sells sparingly. He goes further: a consecrator is also sparing and keeps the land. So he cannot be explained as following רבי עקיבא.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, it is obvious that he follows the רבנן. And רבי שמעון holds: just as a seller sells sparingly, a consecrator also consecrates sparingly and holds back the land.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא concludes that רבי שמעון agrees with the רבנן about a seller and applies the same sparing rule to a consecrator. This settles the challenge from step 1: רבי שמעון does not follow רבי עקיבא.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי שמעון starts from the רבנן's position that a seller is sparing. He disagrees with them only about a consecrator: for him, a consecrator is sparing too. That is why, in the ברייתא, the land stays with the owner.

keyTerms.meaning: And he holds back the land for himself

phrases.english: Rather, it is obvious that he follows the Rabbis,
and Rabbi Shimon holds:

phrases.aramaic: כִּי הֵיכִי דְּמוֹכֵר בְּעַיִן רָעָה מוֹכֵר,
phrases.english: just as a seller sells sparingly,
one who consecrates also consecrates sparingly,
and he holds back the land.

steps.whatToRemember: רבי שמעון = like the רבנן about a seller (sparing), and he extends it to a consecrator (also sparing). So he cannot be explained as following רבי עקיבא.
steps.whyThisMatters: This knocks down the earlier attempt to line up רבי שמעון with רבי עקיבא. It also clarifies a three-way split: רבי עקיבא is generous for both, the רבנן split between seller and consecrator, and רבי שמעון is sparing for both.
steps.triggerLanguage: אֶלָּא פְּשִׁיטָא אַלִּיבָּא דְרַבָּנַן, וְקָא סָבַר רַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers step 6 and thereby completes the challenge raised in step 1.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: רבי שמעון follows the רבנן that a seller sells sparingly, and holds that a consecrator is also sparing and keeps the land. The suggestion that he follows רבי עקיבא is refuted.
